title: Should you run in the rain? The math says: barely
description:
Split yourself into two targets. Your head and shoulders catch rain for every second you're out, so running 3 times as fast cuts that to a third. But your front sweeps up every drop hanging in the air between you and your door, and that's the same amount whether you walk or run. For 100 m in heavy rain (10 mm an hour, drops falling at 8 m/s, a body 1.75 m by 40 cm): walking 43 mL, running 30 mL, 29% drier. Even infinitely fast, you'd still catch the 24 mL on your front. Physicist Franco Bocci's 2012 study reached the same verdict: in most cases, run as fast as you can.

Numbers checked in code (verify.py), including a simulation of 800,000 raindrops. Sources: Bocci, European Journal of Physics 33, 1321 (2012), as reported by NBC News; drop speed from Wikipedia, Raindrop.

facts_checked: Model: top catches rain rate x top area x time; front catches (rain rate / drop speed) x front area x distance, independent of speed (the standard model, verified by simulation in verify.py). Bocci 2012, 'Whether or not to run in the rain', Eur. J. Phys. 33, 1321: 'in most cases, run', 'running as fast as you can is usually the best way to minimize wetness' (https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna48289836)
Drop fall speed ~8 m/s for 3 mm drops (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raindrop)
100 m at 1.5 m/s = 67 s; at 4.5 m/s (3x) = 22 s; top 18.5 -> 6.2 mL, a third (verify.py)
Front 24.3 mL either way at 10 mm/h; front area 0.70 m2 = 7x top 0.10 m2 (verify.py)
Totals: walk 42.8 -> 43 mL, run 30.5 -> 30 mL, 28.8% -> 29% drier; infinite speed 57% as wet (verify.py)
Simulation of 800,000 drops (400,000 per speed): front the same within 5%, totals ~29% drier (verify.py)
CTA: twice as far, both terms double, still 29% (verify.py)

beats.say: Walk or run in the rain? Running saves just 29%.
You'd think running keeps you way drier. It can't. Some of the rain, you can't outrun.
You're 100 meters from your door, and it's pouring.
Split yourself in two. Your head and shoulders catch rain for every second you're out.
Walking, that's 67 seconds. Run 3 times as fast: 22 seconds. A third of the rain on top.
So running wins by a mile? Look at your front.
Every drop hanging in the air between you and your door ends up on your chest. Walk or run, it's the same drops.
In heavy rain, that's 24 milliliters on your front, either way. And your front is 7 times bigger than your top.
Even at infinite speed, you'd still catch those 24. Running helps. It can't keep you dry.
So if your door were twice as far, would running save you more than 29%?
